reader.requirement: At --std 85, wherever an identifier is qualified (by data-name, file-name, report-name or cd-name, and for the special registers LINAGE-COUNTER, LINE-COUNTER, PAGE-COUNTER), IN and OF are interchangeable, alone or mixed in one qualifier chain, with the same resolution.
reader.edition-search: The grammar spells every qualifier as (OF | IN) (qualification, dataReference's LINAGE/LINE/PAGE-COUNTER arms, reportGroupReference); grep '.IN()' / 'Core.IN' / 'Core.OF' over the compiler finds IN singled out only for the VALUE/EVALUATE 'IN alphabet-name' phrase (DataBinder.RangeAlphabetPhraseOf, EvaluateBinder.BindRangeHigh) and CLASS ... IN, none an identifier qualifier; NameResolution.ResolveQualified and ExpressionFormationPass's qualifier-order check consult no edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: witnesses cover data-name and condition-name qualification; not exercised there are file-name qualifiers, report-name qualifiers of LINE-COUNTER/PAGE-COUNTER, LINAGE-COUNTER IN file-name, mixed IN/OF chains and qualified subscripted references

probes.expected: C OF B = C IN B = 1; C IN D OF A, C OF D IN A, C IN D IN A = 2; C IN TE (1), C OF TE OF T (2), C OF TE IN T (2); condition-name C-ONE IN C OF B; K IN F1 vs K OF R2 (file-name and record qualifiers), ref-mod K IN R2 (2:2); paragraph P2 IN S1, P3 OF S1
LINAGE-COUNTER IN F1 (two writes) differs from LINAGE-COUNTER OF F2 (one write); LINE-COUNTER IN RP1 = 2 vs OF RP2 = 1; PAGE-COUNTER IN/OF = 1

citations.check: OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.5.3 SR1  (4.3.8.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: IN and OF are one grammar alternative in every qualifier position, and resolution never looks at which word was written. No cd-name probe: the communication module was not exercised; the grammar's qualification rule is the same (OF | IN) for any qualifier word.
